title: The Speculative Generality "Rewrite Sandbox"
pattern: Using a legacy system rewrite as a sandbox to introduce trendy, unproven frameworks, programming languages, or highly complex abstractions before delivering basic functional equivalence.
why_bad: It multiplies accidental complexity. Developers spend most of their time fighting the nuances of the new frameworks rather than solving the business problem, leading to delayed releases and eventually project cancelation [43, 100].
detection: A rewritten codebase containing more architectural abstractions (interfaces, traits, factories) and third-party dependencies than the legacy codebase being replaced, while serving the same core requirements.
counterexample: Valid for small experimental prototype projects intended to test the feasibility of a new technology stack (Spike).
fix: Perform rewrites with an investment mindset: keep the rewritten system as simple and minimally abstract as possible, focusing purely on stable domain logic [83, 106, 218].
source: Kill It with Fire, Chapter 1 & 4 [100, 105, 106, 562, 592]; Refactoring to Patterns, "Over-Engineering" [43]
